title: Spatio-Temporal Provenance Guard: Detecting Privilege Escalation Attacks That Exploit Spatio-Temporal Data Loss in Multi-Agent MCP Environments
abstract: Multi-agent systems built on the MCP (Model Context Protocol) let agents of different trust and privilege share records across sessions. The provenance of a record, its source, writer, trust, and privilege, is normally dropped at storage and session boundaries, a loss we call spatio-temporal data loss. This opens a privilege-escalation path: an adversary controlling only an ingestion path can spread an outbound-transfer directive over individually incomplete records that a high-privilege agent later assembles and executes. We propose STPG (Spatio-Temporal Provenance Guard), a gateway defense that persists connector provenance on write, reassembles records by lineage on read, and authorizes privileged routing calls only when a trusted directive is witnessed to target the actual destination and verified against a deterministic support path. On a Google Cloud testbed with Gemini agents, STPG blocked every assembled attack and passed every approved external transfer, whereas a conservative provenance gate blocked all approved transfers and an attribution judge misattributed a fifth of them; it also matched every specified decision on a policy challenge set. Robustness tests locate its limits: literal binding blocks approved calls whose identifier is written differently, and a swapped judge model keeps the gate decisions but lowers detection, while multi-connector attacks remain blocked.

title: Detection of Privilege Escalation in IoT Systems
abstract: <p>Software vulnerabilities in access control models can represent a serious threat in a system. In face, OWASP lists broken access control as number 5 in severity among the top 10 vulnerabilities. In this thesis, we study the permission model of an emerging Smart-Home platform, SmartThings, and explore two approaches of detecting privilege escalation in its permission model. The first approach applies static analysis to extract vulnerabilities by pattern matching. Our second approach is based on model driven engineering (MDE) in addition to static analysis. The second approach complements the static analysis-based approach which cannot analyse the semantic itself. MDE-based approach allows for better coverage of privilege escalation, by analyzing free-form text that carries extra permissions details. Our experimental results demonstrate a very high accuracy for detecting vulnerabilities in both approaches.</p>

title: A Prime-Factorization Invariant for Classifying Cyclic Privilege Escalation in Cloud IAM
abstract: Non-human identities (NHIs) in cloud environments may form strongly connected components (SCCs) that defeat existing automated policy analysis tools and require costly manual review. We introduce the primorial invariant: a canonical encoding of SCC cycle structure that enables automated classification of cyclic privilege patterns into three actionable categories: reduction (benign cycles that can be collapsed), fusion (structurally equivalent cycles that share a single analyst decision), and fusion-reduction (approximate variants that can be jointly reviewed and simplified). Unlike attack-graph or black-box learning approaches, the method is lightweight, tolerant to bounded collisions, and designed explicitly for operational scalability rather than perfect discrimination.&nbsp;

abstract: Penelitian ini bertujuan mengidentifikasi dan mengevaluasi teknik privilege escalation pada sistem operasi Linux menggunakan metode Information System Security Assessment Framework (ISSAF) dan taktik dari MITRE ATT&CK. Pengujian dilakukan pada lab VulnHub Lin.Security yang rentan. Tahapan meliputi perencanaan (konfigurasi VirtualBox), assessment (enumerasi sistem dan pengujian 7 taktik MITRE ATT&CK: Abuse Elevation Control Mechanism, Account Manipulation, Create or Modify System Process, Escape to Host, Event Triggered Execution, Exploitation for Privilege Escalation, Hijack Execution Flow), dan pelaporan. Hasil menunjukkan ketujuh taktik berhasil dieksploitasi pada lingkungan lab, mengungkap kerentanan seperti miskonfigurasi SetUID/SetGID, sudo, SSH keys, systemd, docker SUID, file konfigurasi shell, kerentanan kernel (PwnKit), dan LD_PRELOAD. Kesimpulan utama adalah kerentanan privilege escalation pada sistem Linux dapat dieksploitasi menggunakan taktik MITRE ATT&CK, menekankan pentingnya audit keamanan dan pembaruan berkala untuk mitigasi risiko. Kata Kunci: Privilege Escalation, ISSAF, MITRE ATT&CK, Linux, Keamanan Sistem Operasi, VulnHub.

The Confused Deputy in the Swarm: Cascading Privilege Escalation and Memory Poisoning in Multi-agent LLMs
abstract: Multi-agent Large Language Model (LLM) systems divide complex workflows across specialized subagents with different privilege levels. While prompt injection is widely studied in standalone LLMs, trust dynamics across inter-agent communication channels and stateful memory hierarchies remain largely unexplored. This paper presents an empirical laboratory study investigating two primary attack vectors in heterogeneous swarms: Cascading Privilege Escalation across Inter-Process Communication (IPC) and Latent Memory Poisoning within Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) vector stores. Using an isolated benchmark testbed with open-weights models (SmolLM2-135M, Qwen2.5-0.5B/1.5B, and Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct), we demonstrate that subordinate worker agents refine and concentrate indirect prompt injections rather than diluting them. This behavior drives cascading escalation rates up to 65.0% in downstream orchestrators. Furthermore, poisoned memory vectors reliably trigger multi-step Chain-of-Thought reasoning drift (RTR = 75.0%). While prompt-level mitigations cause severe over-refusal, deterministic non-LLM policy firewalls completely eliminate escalation while preserving baseline task utility. All testbed code and raw trial transcripts are fully anonymized and included in the supplementary material for peer review. title: Security Analysis of Browser Artificial Intelligence Panel Privilege Escalation Vulnerability
authors: Fadly Kasim; Muhammad Yahya; Bakhrani Rauf; Taufiq Nasir
abstract: Abstract                   The integration of artificial intelligence (AI) assistants into web browsers introduces new attack surfaces that existing browser security models were not designed to address. This paper presents a systematic security analysis of CVE-2026-0628, a high-severity (CVSS 8.8) privilege escalation vulnerability in Google Chrome arising from inconsistent privilege enforcement in the Gemini Live AI side panel. Unlike standard browser tabs, the AI panel context inherits browser-level privileges including access to local files, camera, and microphone without enforcing adequate isolation from third-party extensions. Through analysis of Chrome’s declarativeNetRequest API behavior, context comparison based on vendor disclosures, and an automated permission audit of 114 unique Chrome Web Store extensions across five categories using a dual-methodology classification (single-dimensional rule and multi-dimensional weighted scoring), we demonstrate that the AI panel creates a privilege boundary gap exploitable by extensions holding only basic permissions. Both methods converge on the same finding: of 46 successfully analyzed extensions, 73.9% held permission combinations sufficient to exploit this boundary gap, substantially higher than previously reported over-privilege rates. The <all_urls> match pattern appeared in 70.6% of high-risk extensions. We identify a security paradox in the security/privacy category (80.0% high-risk) and propose three mitigation strategies for AI feature integration in browsers.

title: ESCALATE: A paired synthetic dataset of safety-critical clinical escalation conversations generated using multi-agent large language models​
abstract: ESCALATE is a structured synthetic dataset of 480 multi-turn clinical escalation conversations organised into 240 matched control–ISBAR pairs. These comprise 200 primary experimental pairs and 40 additional nurse-in-charge pairs generated from a pre-specified subset of the primary scenarios. Each pair was instantiated under two communication conditions: unstructured escalation and escalation guided by the Identification, Situation, Background, Assessment and Recommendation (ISBAR) framework. Role-constrained large language model agents represented a ward nurse and medical registrar, with a nurse-in-charge role included where specified by the scenario design. Records preserve the complete turn-level transcript together with case metadata, communication condition, model provenance, expected information and actions, and structured safety- and quality-related evaluation fields. The paired design permits within-case analysis of information transfer, unsupported clinical inferences, omissions, management-plan actionability, closed-loop communication and conversational efficiency while holding the underlying case constant. The records are distributed in machine-readable JSONL format through Zenodo and Hugging Face under a CC BY 4.0 licence. ESCALATE can support benchmarking of conversational clinical artificial intelligence, development and comparison of dialogue-evaluation methods, information-flow analysis and simulation-based education research. The conversations are entirely synthetic and are not intended to provide clinical guidance or direct clinical decision support.

title: Eurowhiteness in Science: Privilege Escalation and Intentional Sludge
Rejection-Induced Confabulation Escalation -Pilot Study 2 (RICE-P2): Source-Request Framing and FCR Position Modulate URL Fabrication in Large Language Models
abstract: Source fabrication-the generation of plausible but nonexistent citations by large language models (LLMs)-poses a practical problem in information-seeking contexts. Prior work (RICE-P1) found that quality challenges do not escalate fabrication; the present study (RICE-P2) examines whether FCR position and source-request framing modulate fabrication rates. In a pre-registered 16-arm factorial experiment (N = 1,280 runs; 40 fictional entities; 2 platforms), we tested ChatGPT and Perplexity AI using automated content-based URL annotation as the primary endpoint (BSE@FCR: Bad Source Exposure at First Citation Request). Results revealed a near-total platform divergence: Perplexity produced bad sources in 100% of FCR-arm runs (600/600), ChatGPT in 15.7% (94/600; Fisher's exact p &lt; 0.001). Among ChatGPT runs, fabrication increased with FCR delay (Mann-Whitney p = 0.010), SAFE framing eliminated fabrication entirely (BSE = 0%, p = 0.0004 vs. standard), QUOTA framing tripled fabrication rates (70% vs. 28%, p &lt; 0.001), and a quality challenge immediately before the FCR suppressed fabrication by 80% (OR = 0.20, p = 0.003). Claim-mapping framing (CLAIMMAP) was null on BSE but reduced Perplexity's False Source Rate by 50-74%. Source fabrication is powerfully architecture-dependent and is modulated by prompt framing and conversational context at the moment of the source request.
